skills.mechanics_boundary: 200-Ki Ki Blast Super from PQ145. The user holds one hand flat and fires a 13-hit barrage of Ki bullets; holding the input increases projectile size and damage. Current evidence identifies long-range projectile behavior and knockback. Exact charge scaling, startup, recovery, and damage curve remain unresolved.

Character-exclusive Other Super/charge skill used by Mira (Final Form) in Crystal Raid content. Current evidence describes an Afterimage-like warp in place before charging, followed by a rapid Ki increase; independent reference material reports automatic stopping after six Ki bars. The six-bar endpoint is retained as source-reported evidence, while exact charge rate, timing, and usage limits remain unresolved.

100-Ki Strike Super from PQ135. The user pirouettes in place to draw opponents inward; the full move can reach 20 hits and applies a guard-Stamina-depletion effect after the sequence connects. Additional input cancels into a forward tackle that deals at least 3% source-reported damage. Exact frames, reward probability, and detailed scaling remain unresolved.

100-Ki Ki Blast Super from Captain Ginyu mentor Lesson 2. The projectile initially travels quickly, then slows and remains in the air for roughly three seconds; charging changes the distance at which the slowdown occurs. Current skill documentation reports a single hit, knockback, and about 10% damage. Exact charge timing and projectile-speed curve remain unresolved.

500-Ki Strike Ultimate sold through the TP Medal Shop. The user kicks, punches, and then produces a Shenron-image piercing attack; current Xenoverse 2-specific documentation records 14 hits and about 50% total damage. The follow-up can fail if the sequence is interrupted or avoided. Exact startup, recovery, and hit-confirm windows remain unresolved.

300-Ki Ki Blast Ultimate from PQ154. The user rushes forward through a rapid multi-hit sequence, then launches a blue energy attack; additional input makes the user vanish and reappear behind the opponent for another attack. Current reference material reports 21 hits and about 40% total damage, both retained as source-reported values.

100-Ki Ki Blast Super associated with Android 18 (DB Super) and acquired through PQ165 under the repository's explicit 45% Ultimate Finish route. Current evidence documents multiple input variations, including a charged overhead shot and a back-jump shot. The maintained reward data also presents a conflicting Basic Reward listing; that source conflict remains explicit.

300-Ki Ki Blast Ultimate from PQ147. The user throws two initial Ki blasts; if both connect, a larger Ki wave follows for a source-reported 30% total damage. Back input before the first throw sends the first projectile behind the user, after which the move continues normally. Exact projectile timing, scaling, and reward probability remain unresolved.
